facts.text: Eskridge was platted in 1868 by Colonel Ephraim H. Sanford, who named the town after his friend Charles V.
Eskridge City Park, founded in 1903 on donated land, hosts an octagonal wooden bandstand built around 1908–1909 and earned National Register status in 2017.
The arrival of the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway in 1880 turned Eskridge into a cattle shipping hub, with the county leading Kansas in 1898 shipments.
Eskridge faced repeated fires, including a 1909 bakery blaze that destroyed five businesses and a 1913 conflagration that razed nine Main Street buildings.
A post office opened on October 18, 1869, marking Eskridge’s formal recognition and early community with a store, tavern, and stage station.
Eskridge sits atop a 1,700‑foot plateau, giving it a higher elevation than many surrounding towns.
